answer: Reputation decay pricing: each identity’s standing decays on a fixed pulse, so maintaining a credible signal of activity requires recurring, non-recoverable spend that grows with the number of identities. An attacker can mint many keys, but each must pay a separate jade renewal fee—concrete per-identity cost—plus transaction fees to keep its score above threshold. Collusion raises the marginal cost superlinearly because cross-identity interactions must be repeatedly paid for, not simulated once.
